name: merks-ecm-reciprocity-2d
title: Cell-ECM mechanical reciprocity (Merks 3D CPM-ECM, reproduced in 2D with the real engine)
lead:
The 3D target paper has no public code and runs on a GPU/HPC cluster. Rather
than reimplement it, this investigation bridges the actual published 2D
engine it descends from (Tsingos 2023) and runs it on a laptop via Docker,
then asks how much of the 3D paper's story the real 2D ancestor reproduces.
The honest answer: the mechanisms reproduce clearly; the quantitative
equilibrium figures need model calibration that is documented, not faked.

at_a_glance.role: Real coupled run (single contractile cell): the cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM (13135->~10 lattice sites) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 1.00->~1.09). Reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's Fig 4 remodeling; the ECM-limited equilibrium magnitude (Fig 2) is a documented calibration gap, not claimed.

Real crosslink sweep: giant-component fraction jumps from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) to ~0.29 (>=1600 created) — the percolation-ONSET mechanism of Fig 2B. Saturates below full percolation at these reduced densities; the onset direction is the claim, not a percolation-threshold value.

how_to_read:
Start with the verdict above. Each study's interactive figure is built from
REAL engine output (no synthetic data). 'Mechanism-confirmed' means the
direction/qualitative behavior matches the paper; it is deliberately NOT a
claim of quantitative figure reproduction. The two 'evidence_against' points
and the calibration gap are the honest limits, not footnotes.

glossary.definition: The real 2D hybrid cellular Potts + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023), TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3. Bridged by viva-tstmd and run CPU-only via Docker.
Cells deform/remodel the ECM while the ECM's mechanics shape the cell — the mutual coupling this investigation reproduces.
Fraction of fibers nearly radial to the cell (alignment gamma>=0.9, paper eq. 7) over its initial value; >1 means fibers reorient toward the cell.
Fraction of ECM beads in the largest connected component of the bond+crosslink graph; a percolation measure (paper Fig 2B).

The quantitative equilibrium figures (Fig 2 magnitude, Fig 3) are not reproduced because mapping the authors' physical-unit parameters to the engine's internal units is unsolved here. Documented, not tuned away.

biological_story:
Cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) are in constant mechanical dialogue.
A cell anchors to the surrounding fiber network through adhesions and pulls:
the ECM resists, deforms, and remembers — fibers reorient toward the cell and
the matrix densifies locally. That resistance in turn shapes how far the cell
can contract or spread. This mutual push-and-pull, "mechanical reciprocity,"
is how tissues set their form in development, wound healing, and cancer
invasion.

The stiffness of the matrix is not a fixed material constant — it is built by
crosslinks that tie neighboring collagen fibers together. Below a critical
crosslink density the network is a loose collection of disconnected strands
that a cell can rearrange freely; above it, the fibers form a single connected
(percolated) scaffold that transmits force over long range and genuinely
resists the cell. Crosslinking is thus the knob that converts a floppy gel
into a load-bearing tissue.

This investigation watches that dialogue directly in a real simulator: a
contractile cell embedded in a crosslinked bead-spring ECM. We see the cell
contract and drag nearby fibers into radial alignment (reorientation), and we
see crosslinking knit the loose network into a connected scaffold (the onset
of percolation) — the two sides of the reciprocity the Merks-lab models were
built to study.
question:
Can we reproduce the cell-ECM mechanical-reciprocity phenomena of Keijzer &
Merks 2026 (arXiv:2609.02375, a 3D hybrid cellular Potts model coupled to a
discrete deformable fiber network — code unreleased) by driving the REAL
published 2D ancestor engine (Tsingos et al. 2023 static-adhesion TST-MD)
on ordinary hardware?
hypothesis:
The 3D paper extends a published, open 2D engine. Bridged and run CPU-only,
that real engine should reproduce — at the mechanism level, in 2D — the same
reciprocity phenomena: a contractile cell deforms a crosslinked bead-spring
ECM, fibers reorient toward the cell (q/q0 > 1), and crosslinking builds
network connectivity (percolation).

acceptance_criteria.behavior: On the real engine, a contractile cell contracts to <10% of its initial area AND aligns nearby fibers toward itself (q/q0 >= 1.05 at peak and final), reproducing the direction of Keijzer & Merks 2026 Fig 4. The ECM-limited equilibrium magnitude of Fig 2 is explicitly NOT claimed (documented calibration gap).

On the real engine, introducing crosslinks raises the giant-component fraction by >10x over the uncrosslinked network (0.0007 -> 0.18 at onset), reproducing the percolation-onset mechanism of Fig 2B. Full percolation (~1.0) is NOT claimed at these reduced densities.

executive.what_is_this:
A real-engine, 2D reproduction of the mechanical-reciprocity phenomena in a
recent (unreleased) 3D cell-ECM model from the Merks lab. The deliverable
has two parts: (1) viva-tstmd — a reusable process-bigraph bridge that runs
the genuine TST-MD simulator (TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3) CPU-only inside
Docker, with 19 tests; and (2) this investigation, which uses it to measure
the paper's observables on real runs. It is framed deliberately as a
mechanism-level reproduction, not a quantitative figure match.
executive.verdict:
The infrastructure goal is fully met and the MECHANISMS reproduce; the
quantitative equilibrium figures do not yet, and that gap is characterized
rather than hidden.

What reproduces, from real runs of the real engine (2D):
  * Contraction — a contractile cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM
    (cell area 13135 -> ~10 lattice sites over ~80 MCS).
  * Reorientation — the contracting cell aligns nearby fibers toward itself
    (q/q0 rises 1.00 -> ~1.09 and holds), matching the DIRECTION of the 3D
    paper's Fig 4.
  * Connectivity — crosslinking sharply raises network connectivity
    (giant component 0.0007 -> 0.18 -> ~0.29), the percolation ONSET behind
    Fig 2B.

What does NOT yet reproduce (documented calibration gap): the quantitative
equilibrium relationships — Fig 2's equilibrium-area-rises-with-crosslinking
and Fig 3's stiffness drag. Across ~9 real probe simulations a fully
contractile cell collapses to ~0 at every tractable regime, and the network
saturates below full percolation. The authors' calibrated parameters
(Keijzer 2025, Table 1) are in physical units requiring a non-trivial
scaling to the engine's internal units, and their published experiments are
cell SPREADING (a dynamic-focal-adhesion phenomenon) rather than the 3D
paper's static-adhesion contraction. Closing this is model-calibration
research, flagged as the open next step — no constant was tuned to fake a fit.

decisions_needed.question: Invest in physical->ymmsl unit-scaling calibration to reproduce the quantitative Fig 2/3 equilibrium figures?
decisions_needed.context: Would require deriving the scaling from Keijzer 2025 Table 1 + the K=YA/L relations and near-paper-scale sweeps. Open-ended; the mechanism-level result stands without it.

scientific_argument.main_claim: The real published 2D engine, bridged and run on a laptop, reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's cell-ECM reciprocity phenomena (contraction, fiber reorientation q/q0>1, crosslink-driven connectivity); the quantitative equilibrium magnitudes are a documented calibration gap.
evidence_for: Connectivity: giant component 0.0007 -> ~0.29 with crosslinking, percolation onset of Fig 2B (tstmd-network-connectivity).
The engine is the REAL TST-MD (not a reimplementation/mock); 19 bridge tests pass.
evidence_against: A fully contractile cell collapses to ~0 at all probed regimes — no quantitative Fig-2 equilibrium-vs-crosslinking trend yet.
Network saturates at giant component ~0.29, short of full percolation (~1.0) at tractable densities.
key_figures: tstmd-contraction-reorientation: contraction + q/q0 time series with start/end ECM snapshots.
tstmd-network-connectivity: giant component vs crosslinks created.
caveats: 2D (engine) vs 3D (target paper): mechanism/direction analog, not a dimensional match.
Static adhesions (as the 3D paper uses), not the dynamic focal adhesions of Keijzer 2025.
Reduced sizes for CPU tractability; single seed per condition.
Quantitative equilibrium figures (Fig 2 magnitude, Fig 3) require unit-scaling calibration — not attempted/claimed here.

studies.name: tstmd-contraction-reorientation
studies.title: Cell contraction & fiber reorientation (real TST-MD, 2D)
studies.question: In the real 2D static-adhesion hybrid CPM + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023, the published ancestor of Merks' 3D model), does a contractile cell contract against a crosslinked ECM and reorient the surrounding fibers toward itself, reproducing the direction of the 3D paper's remodeling result?

evidence.from_test: Contractile cell contracts against the ECM

findings.statement: The real TST-MD engine reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's remodeling result in 2D: a contractile cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 1.00 -> ~1.09).

At this parameter regime the cell's equilibrium area is set by its target area (10), not by ECM resistance — so this study demonstrates the contraction + reorientation MECHANISM, not the quantitative ECM-limited-equilibrium relationship of Fig 2. Closing that gap requires model calibration (physical->ymmsl unit scaling); documented as the investigation's open calibration item.

studies.claim: The real engine reproduces, in 2D, the direction of the 3D paper's mechanical-reciprocity result: a contractile cell contracts (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites over ~80 MCS) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 rises 1.00 -> ~1.09 and holds).

derived.insight: The real TST-MD engine reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's remodeling result in 2D: a contractile cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 1.00 -> ~1.09).

key_metrics.label: Contractile cell contracts against the ECM
Fibers reorient toward the contracting cell (q/q0 > 1)

studies.name: tstmd-network-connectivity
studies.title: Crosslinking builds ECM network connectivity (real TST-MD, 2D)
studies.question: In the real 2D bead-spring ECM engine, does increasing the number of crosslinks raise the connectivity (giant component) of the fiber network, reproducing the percolation mechanism that underlies Fig 2B of Keijzer & Merks 2026?

evidence.from_test: Crosslinking connects the fiber network (percolation onset)

findings.statement: Crosslinking sharply raises ECM network connectivity: the giant component jumps from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) to 0.18 at ~400 crosslinks and ~0.29 at >=1600 — the percolation-onset mechanism behind Fig 2B.

Connectivity saturates near 0.29 at these reduced fiber/crosslink densities rather than reaching full percolation (~1.0 at the paper's HPC scale). The ONSET direction is reproduced; the full percolated regime needs near-paper-scale networks (a documented scope/calibration limit).

derived.insight: Crosslinking sharply raises ECM network connectivity: the giant component jumps from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) to 0.18 at ~400 crosslinks and ~0.29 at >=1600 — the percolation-onset mechanism behind Fig 2B.

key_metrics.label: Crosslinking connects the fiber network (percolation onset)
